alert.finding: Proof 1.1 defines g* as the pointwise limit on the convergence set and zero elsewhere. Proof 2.1 then says: “For ε>0, every point of D_{m,k} belongs to the positive-maximal set of (g−(k/m−ε))1_{D_{m,k}}.” The universal pointwise assertion need not hold on the exceptional null set assigned g*=0. For example, take X={p} disjoint union {1,2,...}, give p probability one and every integer probability zero, set T(p)=p, T(j)=j+1, g(p)=0 and g(j)=−j². This is a finite measure-preserving system with integrable finite-valued g. The averages diverge to −∞ on every integer, so the prescribed g* is zero everywhere and D_{m,0}=X. With ε=1/2, every partial sum of g+ε starting at an integer is negative, so those points are outside the positive-maximal set. The missing qualification concerns only a null set and does not undermine the integral conclusion.
